read_from: route text as served (reader/data/route-store on main, store_version from its index.json); in this dictionary the route equals the definition field on every row read; the source's own key to its signs is the Open Scriptures lexical index's notes, which use '(from the margin)' for the qere

shapes.means: ends the name before the index's own cross-reference word, Compare or See; the reading is the name and the pointer is not a reading
shapes.test: a period at top level followed by optional space and then the word Compare or See

shapes.means: ends the name before a parenthetical note the record cuts off; nothing after it is read
shapes.test: a period at top level followed by optional space and an opening parenthesis

shapes.means: opens the note that this name is the form written in the margin (the qere)
shapes.test: an opening parenthesis whose group is exactly the words from the margin

shapes.means: closes the note that this name is the form written in the margin
shapes.test: a closing parenthesis whose group is exactly the words from the margin

shapes.means: opens letters that may be added to the name, a gentilic or plural ending: Mede(-s)
shapes.test: an opening parenthesis whose group is a hyphen followed by lowercase letters only

shapes.means: closes the letters that may be added to the name
shapes.test: a closing parenthesis whose group is a hyphen followed by lowercase letters only

shapes.means: attaches the ending to the name with no space, so Mede(-s) reads Mede or Medes
shapes.test: a hyphen inside parentheses whose whole group is a hyphen and lowercase letters

shapes.means: opens a short English remark about the name, such as including the article
shapes.test: an opening parenthesis whose group is lowercase words and spaces and not the margin note

shapes.means: closes the short English remark about the name
shapes.test: a closing parenthesis whose group is lowercase words and spaces and not the margin note

shapes.means: an opening parenthesis the record never closes; the note is cut off and nothing after it divides
shapes.test: an opening parenthesis with no matching closing parenthesis anywhere after it

homonyms.reason: the index gives one name per entry and no entry number; of the 4 letters keys that carry more than one text, Shamir (from the margin) beside Shamir. Compare is one name in two notes, and Elihoenai beside Elienai is two spellings: telling a true homonym from a second note needs the record id, which the route text does not carry

not_done_here: nothing in this dictionary divides readings: every route is one name with notes about it
